plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. My value is $3. If I bid $3 and win, I pay the second-highest bid which is less than $3, ensuring non-negative profit. If I bid higher, I risk overpaying (winning at a price above my value). If I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Bidding exactly my value maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding your value maximizes expected profit: if you bid higher, you risk winning when value < payment; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid truthfully at $24.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value risks negative profit, and bidding below reduces my chance of winning without improving the price I'd pay. With no prior round history to adjust for opponent tendencies, the optimal and risk-free strategy is to bid exactly my value of $11.
